clue.text: Disreputable yob mostly seen with guerrilla leader

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word is kept, its final letter dropped

parts.note: a yob is a lout, a loutish youth
Che Guevara, the Argentine-born guerrilla leader of the Cuban revolution

explanation.surface: A shady character: a thug hanging around with a revolutionary commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims LOUT to LOU; then add CHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Louche describes someone of dubious morals, a shady, seedy sort of person.

clue.text: Its blades are designed to cut down others

definitions.text: Its blades are designed to cut down others

parts.words: Its blades are designed to cut down others
parts.note: a machine whose rotating blades trim blades of grass

explanation.definitionFit: A garden machine with rotating blades used to cut the grass, whose leaves are also called blades.

clue.text: One is made if one does this!

definitions.text: One is made if one does this!

parts.words: One is made if one does this!
parts.note: to join several things into a single whole literally makes one

explanation.definitionFit: To unify is to bring things together into a single whole, making them one.

clue.text: Theatre, of course, no longer in use

definitions.meaning: a music hall or variety theatre

definitions.text: of course, no longer in use
definitions.meaning: in ancient Greece and Rome, a course for horse and chariot races

explanation.definitionFit: Many variety theatres took the name; originally it was the ancient Greek racecourse for horses.

clue.text: Widespread complaint about the same Hollywood spectacular

indicators.note: about means the film word goes around the Latin word for 'the same'

parts.note: an epic is a lavish big-budget Hollywood film
idem is Latin for 'the same', used in references

explanation.surface: Grumbling over the same old lavish blockbuster film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' is an illness, not a grumble; 'about' sets the Latin word inside the film word.
explanation.definitionFit: An epidemic is a disease spreading widely through a population, an illness found everywhere.

clue.text: Petty formality is curiously unpolitic

indicators.note: curiously signals the letters of the next word are oddly reordered

explanation.surface: A remark that fussy etiquette is strangely tactless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curiously' rearranges UNPOLITIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A punctilio is a fine point of etiquette or ceremony, a minor nicety of conduct.

clue.text: Stainer's' dreadful sound

indicators.note: sound says the word for dreadful is heard aloud, not spelt

parts.note: dire means dreadful

explanation.surface: A complaint that someone's colouring work is awful-sounding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stainer's' reads as 'Stainer is': a stainer is dreadful-sounding.
explanation.definitionFit: A dyer colours cloth, so stains it, a stainer by trade.

clue.text: Crooked aims of one group of criminals

indicators.note: crooked means twisted, so the letters are bent into a new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Bent intentions of a single gang of crooks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crooked' rearranges AIMS OF I.
explanation.definitionFit: Mafiosi are members of the Mafia, a gang of organised criminals.

clue.text: Small room associated with old music-maker

parts.note: a cell is a small room, as in a prison or monastery

explanation.surface: A tiny chamber linked with an ancient minstrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A cello is a large stringed instrument, something that makes music.

clue.text: Eyesore installed in the middle of last year

indicators.note: the letters are set within the middle of the next two words

explanation.surface: An ugly building put up halfway through the previous year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eyesore' looks like an ugly sight, but it is literally a sore on the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, a sore on the eye.

clue.text: Sounds like a cruel way to treat a dog

indicators.note: sounds like says the phrase is heard, not spelt, giving the dog's name

parts.words: a cruel way to treat a
parts.note: to treat a dog cruelly is to 'whip it'

explanation.surface: A remark about mistreating a pet with a lash.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'whip it' is the name of the racing dog; the dog is both the victim in the surface and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A whippet is a slender breed of racing hound, like a small greyhound.

clue.text: Money for poor

definitions.meaning: British slang for cash, what is needed
as an adjective, needy, in want

explanation.definitionFit: British slang calls cash 'the needful'; the word also once meant needy, as in the needful poor.

clue.text: Endless concern about terrible noise in separate flat

indicators.note: about means the trimmed word goes around the rearranged letters
endless means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a concern is a matter, an affair

indicators.note: terrible signals the letters of the next word are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: Worry about dreadful racket from a self-contained apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' leaves MATTE; 'terrible' jumbles the noise into ISONE, and 'about' wraps MATTE round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A maisonette is a self-contained flat, often on two floors, with its own entrance.

clue.text: Player is always up in this game

definitions.text: Player is always up in this game

parts.words: Player is always up in this game
parts.note: in this sport the players are mounted, always up on horseback

explanation.definitionFit: Polo is played on horseback, so every player is always up in the saddle.

clue.text: Amusing person given a lot of lines as warning

parts.note: a caution is old slang for a comic, entertaining person
RY, railway, a network of many lines

explanation.surface: A comedian handed a long script, as a reminder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a caution' is old-fashioned slang for someone amusing or remarkable.
explanation.definitionFit: A cautionary tale is one that warns, so the adjective means serving as a warning.

clue.text: Good-for-nothing lieutenant observed retreating without soldiers

indicators.note: without here means outside, the reversed letters wrapping round the soldiers
retreating means the two pieces before it are read backwards

parts.note: observed means saw
RE, the Royal Engineers, crossword shorthand for soldiers

explanation.surface: A useless officer saw his men fall back and left without troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' turns the officer and the seeing into WASTL; 'without' here means outside, so those letters wrap the engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: A wastrel is an idle, worthless person, a ne'er-do-well.

clue.text: Cavalryman crossing a street in a northern town

indicators.note: crossing means the soldier's word spans the other pieces

parts.note: a lancer is a cavalry soldier armed with a lance

explanation.surface: A mounted soldier crossing a road in a town up north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' sets a street inside the soldier; the result is a city in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancaster is the historic county town of Lancashire in north-west England.

clue.text: Most important cargo crossing Orient

indicators.note: crossing means the cargo word straddles the letter for the east

parts.note: lading is a ship's cargo, as in bill of lading
the Orient is the East, E

explanation.surface: Key freight passing through the Far East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' puts E inside LADING.
explanation.definitionFit: Leading means chief, foremost, first in rank.

clue.text: Protected land held by some Oriental fighters

definitions.meaning: an open zone around a city where building is restricted
a coloured grade in judo and karate

explanation.definitionFit: Britain bans building on open country around cities; martial arts students earn coloured grades.

clue.text: Way of life of various soldiers

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a British army corps
a GI is an American soldier
men are soldiers in the ranks

explanation.surface: How assorted troops live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various soldiers' supplies three different words for soldiers in turn: RE, GI and MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A regimen is a prescribed routine of diet and exercise, a regulated mode of living.

clue.text: Continental citizen providing information on Welshman

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
Evan is a typical Welsh name

explanation.surface: A European supplying intelligence about a man from Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' joins the pieces: in a down light the slang word sits on top of the Welsh name.
explanation.definitionFit: A Genevan is a native of Geneva in Switzerland, a European city.

clue.text: Replace pole cut in a number of parts

indicators.note: replace in the sense 're-place', putting the letters back in a new order

explanation.surface: Instructions to swap a sawn-off pole for a sectioned one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Replace' is an anagram signal: POLECUT rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Octuple means eightfold, made up of eight parts, eight being a number.

clue.text: Bloomer made by university in prudish Us city

indicators.note: in means the letter for university goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: prim means prudish
LA, Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A gaffe committed by a college in a puritanical American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' is not a blunder but a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A primula is a flowering plant such as the primrose, something that blooms.

clue.text: Money used at the Curragh to bet

definitions.meaning: the Curragh is an Irish racecourse
to gamble, put money on a horse

explanation.definitionFit: The Irish pound was called the punt, and to punt is British slang for to gamble.

clue.text: Trial of insurgent leader involved in conspiracy

indicators.note: involved in means the letter is put inside the conspiracy word

parts.note: a plot is a conspiracy

indicators.note: leader means just the first letter of insurgent is taken

explanation.surface: The rebel chief is put on trial for plotting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' gives I, which goes inside PLOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot scheme is a trial run, an experiment before a full launch.

clue.text: Scottish accountant enticed into wrongdoing by compatriot

parts.note: CA, chartered accountant
led on means lured, encouraged into misdeeds
Ian, a typical Scottish name, so a fellow Scot

explanation.surface: A Scottish bookkeeper tempted into crime by a fellow countryman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compatriot' is a fellow Scot, so a Scottish man's name, IAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Caledonia is the old Latin name for Scotland, so Caledonian means of Scotland.

clue.text: Adaptation of Austen novel bringing TV award

definitions.text: Adaptation of Austen novel bringing TV award

parts.words: Adaptation of Austen novel bringing TV award
parts.note: a television adaptation of Austen's novel Emma might win television's top prize, whose name is that title with its last letter changed

explanation.definitionFit: The Emmy is the American television industry's annual award.

clue.text: Smile broadly' when daughter abandons work in mill

indicators.note: abandons means the daughter's letter is dropped from the mill word

parts.note: to grind is what a mill does to grain

explanation.surface: A girl quitting her drudgery at the mill beams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandons' removes D from GRIND.
explanation.definitionFit: To grin is to smile widely, showing the teeth.

clue.text: Young bounder always kept in by obstruction

indicators.note: kept in by means the word for always sits inside the obstruction

parts.note: a let is a hindrance, as in 'without let or hindrance'
ever means always

explanation.surface: A young cad permanently detained behind a barrier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bounder' looks like a cad, but it is a leaping animal; 'kept in by' sets 'always' inside the hindrance.
explanation.definitionFit: A leveret is a hare in its first year, and hares bound along.

clue.text: Amount of drink in American bar

definitions.meaning: a set quantity of spirits served, a tot
in American usage a bar of music is called a ...

explanation.definitionFit: A pub serves spirits in fixed quantities; Americans call a musical bar by the same word.

clue.text: Might they produce any rent after short time?

definitions.text: Might they produce any rent after short time?

indicators.note: after means the rearranged letters follow the abbreviation

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: produce suggests the letters are worked up into something new

explanation.surface: A question about whether tenants will pay rent eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produce' rearranges the rent letters into ENANTRY, put 'after' the time abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenantry is a body of tenants, the people who pay rent to a landlord.

clue.text: Ruler to continue a line

parts.note: a monarch whose role is to carry on a hereditary succession of rulers

explanation.definitionFit: A dynast is a hereditary ruler, a member of a ruling family who keeps a dynasty going.
